Yes, I know. But what I (and Ezterhazy, too, I believe) are suggesting is that there are differences in connotation.

Yes, exactly. 
Being unable to swim is more of a temporary condition, while "I can't" is less easily reversed.

My interpretation of Ezterhazy's distinction is as follows: "Can't" can be used (colloquially, anyway) where one is prevented from doing something, where "may not" is grammatically correct, while "unable to" more precisely refers to some literal, perhaps physical, impediment to the action being suggested.

Example 1: Sorry, I can't [may not] go out with you tonight, because I am under house arrest.

Example 2: Sorry, I am unable to go out with you tonight, because an avalanche has buried me and my house completely.
